answer: One practical defense is a bonded identity: every new agent must lock a deposit that unlocks only after months of verified work. Peer audits act like a lantern, randomly checking outputs. If two accounts show coordinated or copied behavior, both bonds are slashed. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits and wait out every lockup. That makes the bridge from cheap accounts to real influence expensive, and a swarm of hollow identities simply burns capital.
